chewi-optimization-v1.title: Lectures on Optimization
chewi-optimization-v1.rights_boundary: The source has an arXiv non-exclusive distribution grant. No blanket source-text/solution-manual ML reuse license is inferred; only original mathematical restatement, original solutions and bibliographic correspondence enter the Bench. The PDF/render stays outside ML exports.

context_notes: Chapter 3 explicitly assumes C² regularity. The condition-number interpretation uses 0<α≤β and κ=β/α.

The owned APIs generalize Euclidean space to complete real Hilbert spaces, and retain signed-modulus or α=0 intermediate extensions. Those are disclosed API generalizations, not changes to the source exercise.
The answer minimizes a uniform curvature-endpoint bound, not the actual optimal Lipschitz constant of each objective.
unformalized_context: The source's informal large-condition-number iteration-complexity comparison is contextual commentary, not an output of the two named owned declarations.

The finite-dimensional eigenvalue presentation and κ notation are explained in the mathematical answer; the actual owned proofs use the symmetric Rayleigh norm formula and the equivalent (β−α)/(α+β) expression. No separate eigenvalue-list or asymptotic-complexity declaration is claimed.

context_notes: The source uses Definition 1.12's global quadratic upper model, not a gradient Lipschitz hypothesis. The exercise explicitly explains why C² is unnecessary despite the ambient chapter convention.
The reciprocal formula (3.4) and the trial step require β>0. Formula (3.5) and the Lipschitz conclusion remain meaningful at β=0 and have a separate limiting proof.
The Lean results apply on a complete real inner-product space. The source's Euclidean case is a specialization; the full-domain hypothesis makes the trial point admissible.
unformalized_context: The first Lean statement is the squared, scaled form equivalent to (3.4) for β>0. It does not give (3.4) a meaning at β=0.
No separate constrained-domain, converse smoothness or algorithmic convergence result is part of the exercise or its three owned answer bindings.
